correctness.rationale: For each core vertex selected/omitted, proof checks domination and outside-neighbor capacity exactly and establishes iff occupancy inequalities. Every selected-core set is unique; binomial choices determine complete polynomial. Each cluster contributes at least max(1,s+1-k) vertices and explicit constructions attain that. Equality enforces boundary-zero selected cores for \(k\le s\) and boundary at most k-s for \(k>s\), yielding the two exact optimizer counts. The standalone direct adjacency/bitmask enumeration independently checked 857 parameter cases, 75 labeled core graphs and 1,877,184 vertex subsets. Finite testing supports but does not prove the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete size distribution of all k-limited dominating sets, not just the minimum, for the entire arbitrary-core private-clique-corona family. The optimizer classification exhibits a sharp, mathematically natural threshold: componentwise multiplicative rigidity for \(k\le s\) versus bounded outward-core-boundary configurations for \(k>s\), with exact counts and a full high-capacity limit. It reduces a \(2^{n(s+1)}\)-configuration enumeration to a \(2^n\) core-subset expression with polynomial arithmetic in the gadget size; this is a motivated counting and structural refinement of a recently introduced parameter, although exponential dependence on unrestricted core order remains.
